visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: Northgate is worth €300m. It owes €200m of senior loans and €150m of junior bonds. How much do the junior bonds recover?

options.text: 86 cents on the euro
67 cents on the euro
100 cents on the euro
33 cents on the euro

questions.explain: The seniors take their 200 first, leaving 100 for 150 of bonds: about 67 cents. 86 cents is an equal haircut, which isn't how the queue works.
questions.explain_at: Debt isn't one pile, it's a queue

questions.q: In a restructuring, what is the fulcrum security?

options.text: The senior loan, secured on the assets
The class that is owed the most money
The shares held by the old owners
The class where the value runs out

questions.explain: It's the class that is only partly covered by the value of the business. Its holders usually swap their debt for the shares and become the owners.

questions.q: A company is worth more than its debts, but can't refinance a bond due next month. What kind of problem is that?

options.text: A liquidity problem, fixed with time
A solvency problem: someone takes a loss
A reason to file for bankruptcy at once
A reason to sell everything and close

questions.explain: The business is worth more than the debt, so it needs time: an asset sale, new equity, or amend and extend. Court and liquidation come much later.

questions.q: Why did Hertz's shareholders get anything out of its Chapter 11?

options.text: Small investors had bid up the shares
The court split the losses equally
The business was worth more than its debts
Shareholders rank ahead of bondholders

questions.explain: Every creditor was paid in full in cash, and value was left over. The share price rally didn't create that value; the absolute priority rule decided who got it.
questions.explain_at: The business turned out to be worth more than everything it owed

questions.q: Konecta has signed a forbearance agreement with a majority of its lenders. What does that mean?

options.text: The lenders write off part of the loan
The lenders hold off on their rights for now
The lenders swap their loans for shares
The company files for court protection

questions.explain: Lenders agree not to enforce their rights for a while, so talks on the capital structure can go on. Konecta hasn't published how much debt, if any, would be cut.
questions.explain_at: They agree not to enforce their rights for a while
